A_query_half_constant.note: within one condition every trace answers the SAME k queries, so a linear model absorbs E(query) into the bias. The 2048-d trace is effectively 1024-d for ANY linear pooling. The attention network CAN use it (to modulate how each slot is read); concatenation gets that same capability via separate weight blocks, mean-pooling does not.

D_determinism.implication: deterministic -- `5 seeds` has nothing to measure; the config-level bootstrap is the only real uncertainty source

B_concat_order_invariance.note: for a linear model f(x)=sum_i W_i v_i + b, permuting slots permutes the learned blocks; the fitted function is unchanged. D017's concern that concatenation 'would reintroduce a slot-order dependency' holds for a FIXED-weight model, not a fitted one.

C_pooling.note: mean-pooling is the strict special case W_i = W/k for all i: one shared weight matrix across slots, so it cannot tell which query produced which response. Concatenation can. The gap measures how much of the signal needs per-query resolution.
